prechecks: Check Microsoft 365 / Teams service health before changing the physical device.
Check the phone's network link and power source, including PoE state where the model uses PoE.
Check device registration, health and assigned configuration/profile in the Teams Admin Center.
troubleshoot-a-teams-phone-device.rollback: Record the current device configuration/update state before a change. Revert the assigned profile or firmware/update ring only where the platform supports an approved rollback; otherwise use the vendor-supported recovery path.

prechecks: Check room-system power, network link and console error state.
Check device registration/health in Teams Rooms management or the Teams Admin Center.
Check the room resource/mailbox, licensing and sign-in state before resetting the room device.
troubleshoot-a-teams-room-system-offline.rollback: Record meeting policy, room configuration and device state before change. Restore the previous approved policy/configuration if the change makes the room less functional.

prechecks: Check the web-filter/security-gateway log for the exact user, URL, category, rule and reason for the block.
Determine whether the block is a security control for malware/phishing versus a content-category or business-policy restriction.
Compare another authorised user/device to establish scope before requesting an exception.
troubleshoot-a-web-filter-block.rollback: Record the current policy before change. If an approved exception causes wider exposure or incorrect access, remove it and restore the previous policy. Any temporary exception must be authorised, least-privilege and time-bounded.

prechecks: Check client connectivity, posture/compliance state and management-console health.
Check token/session validity and whether the identity is blocked by policy.
Check client logs for connectivity to the organisation's ZTNA/control-plane service.
troubleshoot-a-zero-trust-network-client.rollback: Record the current managed client/profile version. If an approved client/profile update causes regression, restore the previous approved version/profile through the management platform.

prechecks: Check DHCP scope utilisation and available leases before changing the scope.
Check DHCP service health/event logs and failover state where implemented.
Check relay/helper configuration and VLAN gateway reachability when clients are on a different subnet.
troubleshoot-dhcp-address-assignment.rollback: Export or otherwise capture the DHCP server/scope configuration before changing leases, exclusions or failover settings. Before remote Cisco IOS/IOS-XE relay/helper changes, use `reload in 10` and cancel only after DHCP and management reachability are verified; use the vendor-equivalent rollback mechanism elsewhere.

prechecks: This page is a duplicate of the canonical DNS service runbook and must route to it.
Preserve the original symptom mapping and historical URL so existing links do not break.
troubleshoot-dns-name-resolution.rollback: No independent remediation is permitted after deprecation; rollback and change controls belong to the canonical DNS service runbook.

prechecks: Determine whether authentication uses SSH, HTTPS/PAT, SSO or an organisation-managed credential helper.
Check token/key expiry or revocation and repository/group entitlement without exposing secret material.
Test the web interface or another approved authentication path to distinguish account entitlement from local Git configuration.
troubleshoot-git-authentication.rollback: Do not restore revoked or compromised credentials. Record the previous approved credential method/configuration and revert only the client configuration if a new approved credential method causes regression.

prechecks: Check the active resolver configuration (`resolvectl`, NetworkManager or `/etc/resolv.conf` as appropriate) rather than assuming one static file owns DNS.
Test `dig`/`nslookup` against the configured DNS server and an explicit known-good server where policy permits.
Check system time/NTP and DNSSEC-related errors where applicable.
troubleshoot-linux-dns-resolution.rollback: Back up or record the resolver configuration before change and restore the previous approved resolver settings if name resolution worsens.

prechecks: Check Microsoft 365 / Teams service health before local client remediation.
Test Teams on the web to distinguish tenant/account failure from native-client failure.
Check identity state, Conditional Access and device compliance before clearing tokens or profiles.
troubleshoot-microsoft-teams-sign-in.rollback: Record any policy or client-state change. If an approved Conditional Access or configuration change causes wider sign-in failure, restore the previous approved policy/configuration through change control.

prechecks: Test Outlook on the web to confirm mailbox/service health.
Check MDM/Intune compliance, application protection policy and account licensing.
Check the installed Outlook mobile version and managed configuration.
troubleshoot-mobile-outlook-synchronisat.rollback: Record the current managed app/profile state. If an approved app/profile change breaks synchronisation, restore or redeploy the previous approved managed configuration.

prechecks: Check cable/link LEDs, NIC state and physical port before changing software.
Check switch-port VLAN/access configuration and port-security state.
Check STP, errors and MAC-learning evidence when the fault points to the switch rather than the endpoint.
troubleshoot-no-ethernet-connectivity.rollback: Capture the current switch-port configuration before a change. Restore the prior port configuration if connectivity worsens; use the platform's supported remote rollback safety mechanism for switch changes.

prechecks: Check Wi-Fi adapter/driver state and whether the expected SSID is visible.
Check controller/AP association and authentication logs before deleting the client profile.
Check whether the user/device is blocked by 802.1X, NAC, MAC policy or device compliance.
troubleshoot-no-wi-fi-connectivity.rollback: Record the existing managed Wi-Fi profile and driver version. Restore the approved profile/driver if an authorised change causes regression.

prechecks: Start Outlook in Safe Mode to determine whether add-ins are involved.
Record enabled COM/web add-ins and their load state before disabling anything.
Check whether the add-in depends on a network service, authentication or vendor backend.
troubleshoot-outlook-add-ins.rollback: Document each add-in disabled during testing and re-enable only the known-good add-ins after isolating the fault.

prechecks: Test search in Outlook on the web to separate mailbox/service-side search from local indexing.
Check Windows Search/indexing status and whether the mailbox/data scope is indexed.
Check mailbox quota and client health before rebuilding an index.
troubleshoot-outlook-search.rollback: Index rebuild is a regeneration action rather than a reversible configuration change. Warn the user about temporary incomplete search/performance impact and do not delete mailbox data as part of search remediation.

prechecks: Test send/receive in Outlook on the web to confirm mailbox/service health.
Check mailbox quota, message-size limits and whether Outlook is working offline.
Check exact send/receive error, account state and network path before recreating a profile.
troubleshoot-outlook-send-and-receive.rollback: Record the current client/profile/update state before change. Revert only the specific approved client/update/configuration change that caused regression; preserve mailbox data.

prechecks: Try Outlook Safe Mode before profile recreation.
Check navigation-pane/profile and Office activation/licensing state.
Use the Outlook decision links to route launch, send/receive, credential, add-in and search failures to the correct child procedure.
troubleshoot-outlook-that-will-not-open.rollback: Record the current supported Outlook profile/account configuration before recreating it. Restore the previous supported configuration if the replacement fails; do not import untrusted registry/profile material.

prechecks: Capture system, browser and managed proxy/PAC settings before modification.
Confirm the PAC URL is reachable and evaluate whether the expected route is returned.
Compare direct access only where organisational policy explicitly permits it; do not bypass a required security proxy merely to test.
troubleshoot-proxy-configuration.rollback: Restore the previous approved proxy/PAC configuration through the authoritative management source if a change breaks connectivity.

prechecks: Check identity/service health and account/MFA state before deleting cached credentials.
Check the authentication method and whether legacy/basic authentication is being attempted.
Inspect Credential Manager only for relevant stale entries; do not remove unrelated saved credentials.
troubleshoot-recurring-outlook-credentia.rollback: Record relevant credential/cache changes. Restore policy/configuration only through the approved identity/Microsoft 365 configuration path; never restore a compromised or expired credential.

prechecks: Check scanner/MFP network and DNS reachability to the file server.
Check the scanner/service account's share and NTFS write permissions.
Check destination disk/quota capacity and exact SMB/path/authentication error.
troubleshoot-scan-to-network-folder.rollback: Export or record ACL/share and scanner destination settings before change. Restore the previous permissions/path/configuration if scanning worsens; firmware rollback is only permitted where vendor-supported.

prechecks: Determine whether the slowdown is one endpoint, one VLAN/site or provider-wide before treating it as infrastructure.
Check WAN utilisation, loss/latency and provider circuit health.
Check QoS/traffic-shaping and recent WAN/firewall changes.
troubleshoot-slow-internet-access.rollback: Capture QoS, traffic-shaping and WAN-routing state before change. Restore the previous known-good configuration or approved failback path if performance worsens.

prechecks: Trace the application route from the VPN client and confirm which route should be selected.
Check VPN gateway/client route tables and split-tunnel include/exclude policy.
Check firewall/ACL access from the VPN address pool to the application subnet.
troubleshoot-split-tunnel-application-ac.rollback: Capture route/split-tunnel/ACL configuration before change. Remove or revert the specific change if access worsens; use the platform's supported rollback safety mechanism for remote routing changes.

prechecks: Check Microsoft 365 / Teams Phone service health before changing client or calling configuration.
Check licence/calling-plan assignment or Direct Routing/SBC health as applicable.
Capture call ID/time/user and call diagnostics/client logs before policy or SBC changes.
troubleshoot-teams-calling.rollback: Record calling policy, routing and SBC configuration before change. Restore the previous approved policy/routing/SBC configuration if call establishment worsens.

prechecks: Test the camera in the operating system or another approved application.
Check Teams and OS camera privacy/permission settings.
Check whether another application has exclusive access to the camera.
troubleshoot-teams-camera.rollback: Record driver and device settings before change. Restore the previous approved driver/configuration if an authorised update causes regression.

prechecks: Check Microsoft 365 / Teams service health before local remediation.
Test joining through the supported web client to distinguish client from service/network failure.
Check required network/media connectivity and firewall/proxy path, including STUN/TURN-related reachability where relevant.
troubleshoot-teams-meeting-join-failure.rollback: Record firewall/proxy/client changes. Revert only the approved change that caused regression and restore the prior policy/configuration.

prechecks: Check Teams/Exchange service health and mailbox/calendar connectivity.
Check whether the user manually set a presence state and whether it is expected to expire.
Compare web/client presence before clearing local cache.
troubleshoot-teams-presence.rollback: Cache regeneration normally has no meaningful state rollback. Preserve user data and avoid mailbox/calendar deletion; restore the previous client configuration if a configuration change caused the issue.

prechecks: Check meeting role/presenter permission before client remediation.
Check OS screen-recording/privacy permission and monitor/application selection.
Check uplink/media quality and whether application-window sharing works as a controlled comparison.
troubleshoot-teams-screen-sharing.rollback: Record client/permission configuration before change. Restore the previous approved Teams/client configuration if an authorised update or policy change causes regression.

prechecks: Determine whether the queue is local or shared and identify the affected jobs/users.
Check print-server/local disk free space and Print Spooler state before clearing anything.
Capture queue/driver/printer state before stopping services or moving spool files.
clear-a-stuck-windows-print-queue.rollback: Do not immediately delete spool files. Move/copy the affected spool files to an approved temporary evidence/backup location where policy permits, clear only the affected queue, and restore the prior queue/service state or escalate if the fault persists.

prechecks: Identify the failing service and the smallest relevant log/time window before collecting.
Collect appropriate journal/system/authentication/application logs plus basic system metadata.
Check whether logs contain secrets, personal data or tokens that require redaction/protected transfer.
collect-linux-logs-for-escalation.rollback: Log collection is read-only and normally needs no rollback. Do not change log retention/rotation merely to collect evidence; remove temporary copies only according to retention policy.

prechecks: Step 0: establish chain of custody: incident/ticket ID, asset, collector, date/time/timezone, evidence source and transfer location.
Preserve volatile evidence before reboot/destructive remediation where authorised; capture memory only with approved forensic tooling and trained personnel.
Export relevant EDR/SIEM/event/email/identity/network evidence to an approved protected location and record cryptographic hashes.
collect-security-incident-evidence.rollback: Evidence preservation is intentionally non-reversible. Do not modify original evidence to undo collection. Protect originals, hash copies with SHA-256 or the organisation's approved algorithm, and document every custody transfer.

prechecks: Confirm the device is enrolled/eligible for the organisation's MDM and mobile-email policy.
Check required licence and mobile-access/Conditional Access entitlement.
Check Android OS/device compliance and approved Outlook/managed-email app requirements.
configure-corporate-email-on-android.rollback: Record the existing managed account/profile state before configuration. If provisioning fails, remove only the profile/account created by this procedure and redeploy the approved configuration through MDM/Company Portal.
